subject: Order Form pricing floors — clarification on smoothing and proration
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@acmecloud.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmecloud.com
Date: 2028-02-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Clarification: Exhibit B floors/proration behavior

Hi Kimberly / Marissa,

Thanks for sending the updated order form. Our procurement team has a couple of carveouts to clarify before we can route to legal: specifically how the minimum monthly floor in Exhibit B interacts with quarterly true-ups and proration on subscription scale-ups. Two quick questions:

1) If we increase committed tokens mid-quarter, does excess usage above the new commitment during that quarter reduce the floor pro rata, or does the floor apply to the calendar month in which the change occurred?

2) The redline flags a stabilization floor "not to exceed" language — can you confirm whether that phrase was intended to cap the floor adjustment (i.e., ceiling on the stabilization amount) or to cap Redwood's liability to refund?

We've attached a short spreadsheet with a sample ramp scenario. Appreciate a short written answer so our legal can fold it into procurement review.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
VP, Procurement
AcmeCloud

Attachments: OrderForm-Rates-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@acmecloud.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2028-02-15T10:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: Exhibit B floors/proration behavior

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the clear questions and the sample ramp. Short answers first, then a proposed language tweak below.

1) Current drafting applies the floor on a monthly basis. If you increase committed tokens mid-quarter, the floor is pro-rated for the month(s) affected; the quarterly true-up aggregates those prorated months.

2) The "not to exceed" wording was intended as a cap on stabilization adjustments applied to the customer invoice (i.e., to limit upward adjustments to the floor), not as a cap on Redwood refunds. That said, I can see how it's ambiguous.

Proposed clean language (for Exhibit B):
- "Monthly Floor Applicability: The Minimum Monthly Commitment shall be prorated for any change in committed units effective mid-month. Quarterly true-ups will sum the prorated monthly commitments to determine overage/underage."
- "Stabilization Cap: Adjustment to the Minimum Commitment arising from the Stabilization Mechanism shall not increase billed floor liability by more than the lesser of 15% of the prior month’s commitment or $10,000 in the first 12 months following execution."

I'll loop Neha for legal redline precision and Marissa for commercial tolerance. If that cap is a blocker for you, let us know what range you'd need.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Revenue Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment: AcmeCloud-ExhibitB_pricing_redline_v3.pdf (redline PDF)

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@acmecloud.com>, procurement@acmecloud.com
Date: 2028-02-16T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: Exhibit B floors/proration behavior

Kimberly / Marissa / Sanjay — quick legal note to tighten drafting and avoid unintended refunds.

If we keep the monthly proration approach, we should explicitly define:
- the day-of-change rule (changes effective at 00:00 UTC on the change date) to avoid timezone disputes;
- a method for computing partial-month commitments (use actual days in month as denominator); and
- an explicit carveout that stabilization adjustments are applied prospectively (next billing period) except where gross calculation error is identified.

Suggested clause additions: 
"For any increase or decrease in Committed Units, the parties shall compute the prorated Minimum Monthly Commitment by multiplying the baseline monthly commitment by the ratio of days in effect to total days in the month. All Stabilization Mechanism adjustments shall be reflected in the invoice for the subsequent billing period, except where an accounting error resulted in an incorrect historical charge (in which case retrospective correction may be made)."

Neha K. (legal) — ask: would Acme accept a conservative refund-only retrospective correction window limited to 60 days? That helps limit retro liability.

-Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

> > - "Stabilization Cap: Adjustment to the Minimum Commitment arising from the Stabilization Mechanism shall not increase billed floor liability by more than the lesser of 15% of the prior month’s commitment or $10,000 in the first 12 months following execution."

Attachments referenced: AcmeCloud-ExhibitB_pricing_redline_v3.pdf

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@acmecloud.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, procurement@acmecloud.com
Date: 2028-02-17T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: Exhibit B floors/proration behavior

Neha / Kimberly — thanks, that helps a lot. A couple of follow-ups from our side:

- Day-of-change at 00:00 UTC is acceptable.
- For retrospective corrections, Acme's legal prefers a 90-day window rather than 60. Can Redwood do 90 days for refunds/true-ups? Our accounting needs that to reconcile quarterly statements.
- On the stabilization cap, $10,000 feels small for our footprint. Would you consider a tiered cap tied to prior-month spend (e.g., 10% up to $50k, then 5% thereafter)?

If we can land on those, procurement can circulate the revised Exhibit B to our legal and finance.

Sanjay

> On Feb 16, 2028, at 08:22 AM, neha_kapoor@redwood.com wrote:
> > Neha K. (legal) — ask: would Acme accept a conservative refund-only retrospective correction window limited to 60 days? That helps limit retro liability.

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@acmecloud.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2028-02-20T16:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: Exhibit B floors/proration behavior — proposal

Sanjay — appreciate the constructive proposals. Internal alignment: commercial is ok to move to a 90-day retrospective window to match Acme's reconciliation timeline. Legal confirms we should keep the day-of-change 00:00 UTC rule and the actual-days-in-month proration.

On the stabilization cap, we propose the following compromise (keeps predictability for Acme while limiting Redwood downside during onboarding):

"Stabilization Cap (compromise): Adjustments to the Minimum Commitment under the Stabilization Mechanism shall not increase billed floor liability by more than the lesser of (i) 12% of the prior month’s billed commitment, or (ii) $50,000, for the first 12 months following execution. After 12 months, caps revert to standard contract language without a stabilization cap."

If that sounds workable, Kimberly / Neha will incorporate the language into Exhibit B redline and circulate a single tracked PDF for Acme legal + finance review (and we'll include the sample ramp calc you supplied).

Thanks — look forward to a quick thumbs-up.

Best,
Marissa Cole
VP, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
